question: Develop a logistic model for liver cirrhosis. Plan for 24 candidate slope parameters, prevalence 0.17, and anticipated adjusted Cox–Snell R² of 0.288. Use the three Riley binary development criteria: global shrinkage ≥0.90, apparent versus adjusted Nagelkerke R² difference ≤0.05, and a 95% Wald margin of error ≤0.05 for the overall outcome risk. Use z=1.96, do not apply an additional prediction-error criterion, and round up only the final requirements. What minimum number of participants and corresponding expected number of events are needed?

Develop a model for time to first recurrent venous thromboembolism. Assume a constant event hazard of 0.065 per person-year, 30 candidate slope parameters, and anticipated adjusted Cox–Snell R² of 0.051. The prediction horizon is 2 years and mean observed time at risk is 2.07 years per participant. Use the Riley time-to-event development criteria: global shrinkage ≥0.90, apparent versus adjusted Nagelkerke R² difference ≤0.05, and absolute error ≤0.05 at both ends of the 95% confidence interval for the risk at the prediction horizon. For the last criterion, transform both ends of the Wald interval for the constant hazard using standard error √(λ/T) and z=1.96, where T is total time at risk. Use the unrounded expected event fraction in the Cox–Snell maximum calculation. What minimum number of participants and corresponding expected number of primary events are needed?

Develop a linear model to predict fat-free mass in children, on an analysis scale for which the population outcome mean is 1.9 and SD is 0.6. Use 25 prespecified candidate slope parameters and anticipated adjusted R² of 0.20. Center the predictors at their population means. Use Riley's continuous-outcome criteria: global shrinkage ≥0.90, apparent versus adjusted R² difference ≤0.05, a 95% chi-square interval for residual SD with both endpoints within the multiplicative factor 1.10, and a 95% t interval for the mean outcome with half-width ≤10% of the population outcome mean. What minimum total sample size meets all four criteria?

Externally validate a DVT diagnostic model. The predicted log odds L follow N(−1.75, 2.16²). Specify the joint outcome model as Pr(Y=1 | L)=expit(α+βL). Determine α and the positive slope β from the target prevalence 0.22 and C-statistic 0.82, using the given distribution of L. Let the expected component of O/E be the mean model-predicted risk E[expit(L)]. Target 95% interval widths no greater than 0.10 for the C-statistic, 0.20 for the calibration slope, and 0.20 for the O/E ratio. Use Riley et al. (2021) equations 5, 7, and 11, z=1.96, and population integration. Retain the unrounded log-scale O/E standard error and Fisher information. What minimum number of participants and corresponding expected number of events meet these criteria?
